old_description: Founded in 1979 under the name Custom Machining Services, the Valparaiso, Indiana plant is one of the leading U.S. producers of hydraulic hose crimpers, crimping dies and other hose equipment solutions for the hydraulic hose industry. Continental acquired the location on November 1, 2017. With 100 employees, the plant is located about an hour outside of Chicago and known as ‘Valpo’ to local residents.
about:
The Valparaiso, Indiana plant was founded in 1979 as Custom Machining Services, initially serving the hydraulic hose market with custom machining. Continental AG acquired the facility on November 1, 2017, integrating it into the corporation's global industrial portfolio. The site, known locally as "Valpo," sits about an hour southeast of Chicago and operates with approximately 100 employees.

The plant specializes in manufacturing hydraulic hose crimpers, crimping dies, and related hose assembly equipment. Its product line covers crimping machines and tooling designed for hydraulic hose fabrication, serving the fluid power sector. Production includes machining, die forming, and final assembly of crimping systems.

The equipment is sold to hydraulic hose distributors, original equipment manufacturers, and end users in industries such as construction, agriculture, and industrial machinery that rely on hydraulic hose assemblies. The facility's focus on crimping technology positions it as a dedicated supplier within the North American fluid power supply chain.

name: Continental Cable LLC
old_description: Continental Cable is a leading manufacturer of custom steel cable, wire rope, wire rope cable assemblies, cable hardware, and fittings.
about:
Continental Cable LLC was founded in 1969 in Hinsdale, New Hampshire. The company operates as a manufacturer of custom steel cable, wire rope, and related assemblies, serving industrial and commercial markets.

The company produces custom steel cable, wire rope, wire rope cable assemblies, cable hardware, fittings, and plastic-coated cable. Its integrated capabilities include swaging, stranding, extrusion, and machining. The facility employs 65 people.

Continental Cable serves aerospace, military, automotive, agriculture, fire safety, exercise/fitness, marine, medical, telecommunications, and outdoor recreation industries. It is a qualified producer for MIL-DTL-83420 and supplies military and federal agencies.

The company emphasizes its integrated manufacturing capabilities, adherence to strict commercial and government standards, and certifications to AS9100 and ISO 9001. It highlights fast turnaround, competitive pricing, and seasoned industry expertise.

name: Contraxx Furniture
old_description: “Impressive to see the level of craftsmanship and attention to detail in this furniture. Contraxx is a business founded on small town values that delivers world class quality to some of the most discerning clients in America.” – David W.
about:
Contraxx Furniture is based in McConnelsville, Ohio. The company traces its roots to the 1990s when it developed a hub-and-spoke manufacturing system to keep furniture production in the United States. The business grew from a small-town operation into a nationally recognized custom hospitality furniture manufacturer.

Contraxx manufactures custom hospitality furniture including guest room casegoods, beds, seating, banquettes, tables, lobby cabinetry, and bespoke furnishings for hotels, resorts, restaurants, casinos, senior living, and mixed-use properties. Its hub-and-spoke network connects more than 45 family-owned craft shops specializing in woodworking, metal fabrication, upholstery, and finishing, with final assembly and finishing performed in two state-of-the-art factories. The company reports having created over 5,000 skilled jobs in America and operates with no minimum order requirements, backed by a 15-point quality assurance inspection on every product.

The firm serves designers, architects, purchasers, FF&E professionals, and developers across the hospitality sector. Concrete project examples include The Pearl in Nantucket, MA; Elliott House Boutique Hotel in Charleston, SC; Sheraton Grand in Los Angeles, CA; Grand Casinos; Four Seasons; Homewood Suites; and numerous upscale restaurants and bars such as Hank's Seafood, 1587 Prime Steakhouse, and St. Cecilia Restaurant.

Contraxx emphasizes its distributed manufacturing system as a differentiator, enabling efficient production, dependable timelines, and seamless execution at any scale. The company was founded on the belief that furniture manufacturing jobs should stay in America, and it highlights made-exclusively-in-America production, custom design flexibility, turnkey installation, on-site field measurements, and time-critical delivery as core value propositions.

name: Control Components, Inc
old_description: Thank you for visiting Control Components! For 35 years our company has specialized in providing a broad range of factory automation and machine safety solution products from leading manufacturers for the Automotive, Industrial, OEM, and Systems Integrator markets.
about:
Control Components, Inc. operates from Pelham, Alabama, where it has served the factory automation and machine safety market for 35 years. The Alabama corporation is independent of the California-based IMI Critical Engineering entity that shares a similar name. Founded as a specialized supplier, the company built its business around a curated line card of automation components from established manufacturers.

The company functions as an authorized distributor for brands including ABB, GE, IDEC, Eaton, Balluff, Pepperl+Fuchs, Schmersal, and others. Its product range spans sensors (inductive, photoelectric, ultrasonic, limit switches), machine safety devices (light curtains, safety relays, safety switches, safety mats, scanners), control panel components (timers, relays, contactors, circuit breakers, terminal blocks, power supplies), industrial communication (Ethernet switches), and process measurement and control instruments. The Pelham facility maintains supporting inventory and a factory-trained sales staff to assist with product selection.

Control Components targets automotive manufacturers, general industrial plants, OEMs, and systems integrators. Customers source safety light curtains for guarding, inductive proximity sensors for position detection, contactors and starters for motor control, and Ethernet switches for network infrastructure. The company emphasizes its ability to help engineers specify the most cost-effective components for each application.

The firm distinguishes itself through its depth of inventory across safety and automation categories, the technical expertise of its factory-trained personnel, and its status as an authorized channel for multiple major brands. It positions itself as a single-source partner for both standard and specialized automation components.

about:
Control Freaks Hawaii Inc. is based in Kahului, Maui, with a second office in Kurtistown on the Big Island. The company serves residential and commercial clients across the Hawaiian Islands, including Maui, the Big Island, Lanai, Molokai, Oahu, and Kauai.

The firm designs and installs integrated smart home and commercial automation systems. Its services span multi-room audio, home theater, lighting control, motorized window treatments, security, outdoor entertainment, and whole-home automation. It works with platforms such as Control4, Crestron, Lutron, Sonos, and Ketra, and collaborates with builders, architects, and designers from the early design phase. Post-installation support packages are offered to clients.

The client base includes luxury homeowners, second-home owners, and commercial operators in hospitality such as hotels, spas, and condo associations. Trade professionals — builders, architects, and interior designers — regularly engage the company for technology infrastructure planning.

Control Freaks Hawaii emphasizes its Home Technology Association (HTA) certification as a third-party validation of technical competence and service quality. The company highlights personalized design, local community ties, fast turnaround, and ongoing communication as core differentiators.

name: Conway Corp
old_description: Our commitment to the community where we work and live is the reason we were founded. We remain dedicated to enhancing the quality of life in our community through our services, education initiatives and economic development involvement.
about:
Conway Corp has operated from Conway, Arkansas since 1929, when city leaders signed a charter on May 6 to create the municipally owned corporation. The utility began by taking over the city's electric light plant and, within a year, assumed responsibility for waterworks and sewer operations. It remains a public, nonprofit entity governed by a local board, with all revenues reinvested in the community.

The corporation delivers a full suite of utility and telecommunications services: electric distribution, water treatment and distribution, wastewater collection and treatment, cable video, high‑speed internet over a fiber‑coax network, digital voice, and security and automation. It also runs a solar energy program and an IPTV streaming product, ConwayCorpTV. Crews work 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, maintaining substations, treatment plants, and a geographic information system that maps the infrastructure.

Customers are residential and commercial users within the Conway service territory. The utility serves households, local businesses, and municipal facilities, providing both basic utility needs and advanced broadband and entertainment packages.

The founding charter tied the organization directly to community well‑being, a mission reiterated in its core values of customer satisfaction, innovation, safety, reliability, responsibility, and community engagement. Profits are directed back into infrastructure upgrades, education initiatives, and economic development rather than distributed to shareholders.

name: Copeland Furniture Factory Outlet
old_description: Copeland Furniture has been designing and manufacturing natural hardwood furniture for over 50 years, using hardwoods sustainably harvested in the Northeast. We create durable furniture with timeless designs that will last for generations. Visit our Factory Outlet located in Bradford, Vermont to explore our furniture in person.
about:
Copeland Furniture Factory Outlet operates in Bradford, Vermont, as the direct retail arm of a company that has designed and manufactured natural hardwood furniture for more than five decades. The business uses hardwoods sustainably harvested in the Northeast, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not disclosed in public materials.

The outlet showcases the manufacturer's full range of bedroom, dining, living room, and home office collections, all produced from those regional hardwoods. In addition to first-quality pieces, the store stocks factory seconds—items with minor cosmetic flaws—at substantial discounts, with new seconds arriving weekly. The outlet also carries a line of Italian-made mattresses to complement its bed and storage-bed offerings.

The location serves customers across Northern New England and in other regions not covered by the company's independent dealer network. A dedicated Designer Program is available for qualified interior designers, providing trade access to the collections.

The company emphasizes clean design, fine quality, and value, positioning its furniture as durable pieces intended to last generations. The factory-outlet model allows buyers to inspect solid-wood construction in person and take advantage of seconds pricing without waiting for dealer shipments.

name: Corner Woodworks
old_description: Welcome to the home of Corner Woodworks! We build to order, build to suit, and also design in collaboration with you for your space. For our furniture, custom cabinets, and wood countertops we use genuine solid hardwoods combined with modern day joinery and silky smooth hand rubbed finishes that we guarantee to bead water.
about:
Corner Woodworks operates from Manchester, Maryland, where it designs and builds custom wood products for residential and commercial clients. The shop focuses on made-to-order furniture, cabinetry, and countertops using solid hardwoods.

The company produces custom furniture, cabinets, wood countertops, millwork, and butcher block countertops. Each piece is crafted with modern joinery techniques and finished with hand-rubbed oils that penetrate the wood rather than forming a surface film. The shop avoids veneers over fiberboard, using solid hardwood throughout.

Clients engage the shop for collaborative design services, whether for a single piece of furniture or a full kitchen installation. The business serves homeowners, designers, and contractors seeking tailored woodwork built to specific dimensions and aesthetic requirements.

Corner Woodworks differentiates itself through its finishing process, which it says creates a flexible, durable surface that beads water and accentuates the natural character of the wood. The company also emphasizes that all products are manufactured in the United States.
